iut_type: Bluetooth Core Specification version lock-in at registration time -- cannot upgrade an existing registration's declared spec version even if the referenced component is actually higher-spec
customer_question: Our device is currently registered with Bluetooth Core Specification 4.2, even though the QDID we reference actually has Core Specification 5.0. If we want to change our registration to 5.0 without any hardware/software change, would additional testing or special procedures (and cost) be needed?
question_variants: Can an existing registration's declared Core Specification version simply be edited/corrected to match the referenced component's actual spec?
If no testing is needed to move to the higher spec version, is the only cost the new registration fee?
actual_issue: The customer discovered that their existing registration was declared at Bluetooth Core Specification 4.2, despite referencing a QDID whose actual Core Specification is 5.0 -- apparently because the spec version had been deliberately set to 4.2 at the original registration time -- and wanted to upgrade the declared version to 5.0 without any hardware or software change.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG's registration system treats the declared Core Specification version as a value fixed at registration time, not as something dynamically inherited from whatever the referenced QDID's actual spec happens to be. In this case, if the customer hadn't deliberately changed the spec to 4.2 during the original registration, it would have naturally registered at 5.0 by inheriting the referenced QDID's spec -- but because the registration's spec was explicitly set to 4.2 at that time, the registration is permanently treated as a 4.2 registration. SIG's registration operational rules do not allow editing an existing registration's declared spec version after the fact, regardless of what spec the referenced component actually supports. The only way to move to Core Specification 5.0 is to create an entirely new registration referencing the same QDID. However, since the underlying component and its existing test evidence are already 5.0-capable, no new testing is required for this new registration -- it is purely an administrative/application process requiring the standard registration fee (and the corresponding registration support fee if using a proxy registration service).
consultant_answer: Using your existing 4.2 registration as-is and simply changing it to 5.0 isn't possible under SIG's registration operational rules -- once a registration's spec version has been explicitly set, it can't be edited afterward, even though the QDID you reference is actually 5.0. The only path is to create a brand-new registration referencing the same QDID, declared at 5.0 from the start. Since the underlying test evidence remains valid and reusable, no new testing is required -- you'd just need to pay the standard registration fee through that new registration.
decision_logic: When a customer asks to upgrade an existing registration's declared Bluetooth Core Specification version to match a higher-spec referenced component, explain that SIG's operational rules lock the declared spec version at registration time and do not allow it to be edited afterward regardless of the referenced component's actual capability -- the only path is a new registration (reusing existing test evidence, since no hardware/software changed, so no new testing is required, only the standard registration fee).
final_recommendation: When helping a customer scope a registration, flag early that the declared Core Specification version becomes permanently fixed once submitted, even if it doesn't match the referenced component's actual spec -- and that any future desire to use a higher spec version will require an entirely new registration (fee) rather than a correction to the existing one.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer might assume their registration's declared spec version can simply be corrected or upgraded later to match an improved or corrected reference, and be surprised to learn a brand-new registration (and its associated fee) is required instead.
